_readme: Cursor owns these ACP tool identifiers and JSON-RPC method names. The worker and frontend use them to identify subagent launches, to classify the control requests Cursor raises, and to read the extension frames the worker stores on a tool row. LeapMux owns the supplement field name that carries one of those frames into the row's supplemental content, and the `storedTool` keys of the record it builds under the shared ACP `rawOutput` key -- the worker writes that record from Cursor's own transcript and the browser plugin reads it back. `storedBlock` and `blockTypes` identify the transcript block the worker matches by id and the browser plugin then re-reads out of the same record. The nested Cursor-owned fields inside it (`cursor`, `highLevelToolCallResult`, `imageDescriptions`) stay out: the worker copies them without spelling them, so only one language reads them and the contracts rule exempts them. `extensionFrame` holds the fields of the frame stored under `cursorExtension`: the worker writes the method beside its params, and the browser dispatches on that one field instead of guessing the frame from the keys it finds. `toolCallId` and `todos` are the params' own two: the worker matches the frame to a row by the id, and the browser draws the checklist from the rows.

ToolCallID.why: the worker matches the frame to a row by this id BEFORE it stores the frame, so the browser reads the frame off the row it already belongs to and never compares the id again

ToolName.why: the worker matches a block to a row by id alone; the browser reads the name off the matched block to title an MCP result row, which is the only surface that states it

CursorStoredToolOutput.doc:
CursorStoredToolOutput is the record LeapMux builds from Cursor's own transcript
and stores under the shared ACP `rawOutput` key.

`ProviderOptions` keeps Cursor's own nested record whole and unread, because the
frontend owns tool-specific extraction.

CursorStoredExtension.doc:
CursorStoredExtension is what the worker writes into the row's supplemental
content for one `cursor/*` extension frame.

The method rides with the params, so the browser dispatches on one field instead
of guessing the frame from the keys it finds.

CursorExtensionParams.doc:
CursorExtensionParams is the `params` of one `cursor/*` extension frame.

Every one of the three methods states the call it belongs to, and
`cursor/update_todos` adds the rows. The worker matches the frame to a row by the
id; the browser reads the rows back out of the stored frame.

`Todos` stays raw, because the to-do item's own three fields are the shared
to-do vocabulary and not Cursor's. `merge` is absent for the opposite reason:
the worker applies it and the browser deliberately draws no flag from it, so it
is a one-side value that the contracts rule exempts.

CursorToolContent.doc:
CursorToolContent is one block of Cursor's own transcript.

The worker matches a block to a row by id, and the browser plugin re-reads the
same two fields out of the record it stores.
